issues.t: Fuel pump can fail and cut drive power (recall)
issues.sym: The engine may hesitate, lose power or shut off while driving, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: Genesis found the fuel pump on these cars can fail. A software update to the engine computer watches for the problem, and the pump is replaced if it is already failing.
issues.next: Run your VIN through the Genesis or NHTSA recall lookup and book the free repair. If the car has had only the software update and still loses power, go back to the dealer and ask that the pump be checked again.

issues.t: Loss of power from a worn high-pressure fuel pump
issues.sym: Sluggish or lost acceleration, often at low speed or when pulling onto a highway, a rough idle, a check engine light with fuel pressure or 'too rich' codes, or the car going into a reduced-power mode.
issues.why: Genesis issued a service bulletin saying the fuel control valve in the engine-driven high-pressure fuel pump can let in too much fuel as the pump's plunger wears, which upsets the fuel mixture. Owners have reported power loss even after the separate fuel pump recall was done.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the fuel pressure checked by a Genesis dealer. Ask whether service bulletin 25-FL-002G applies to your car. Avoid fast highway merges until it is fixed.

issues.t: Turbo oil feed pipe can leak and cause a fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning-oil smell, oil spots under the front of the car, or oil wetness around the left turbo. Many cars show no sign before the repair.
issues.why: The oil supply pipe to the left turbocharger on the 3.3L twin-turbo V6 can break down and leak oil onto hot engine parts. This recall replaced an earlier one, so cars fixed under the first recall need the newer pipe too.
issues.next: Check for open recalls with your VIN and have the new pipe fitted free. If you smell burning oil or see smoke from under the hood, pull over safely and switch the engine off.

issues.t: ABS module can short and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. Some owners may see an ABS warning light or smell burning from the engine bay.
issues.why: The anti-lock brake control unit can short-circuit inside, which could start a fire in the engine compartment even when the car is parked.
issues.next: Park outside and away from buildings until the free fix (a new fuse for the ABS module) is done. Check your VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: Starter solenoid can short and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning before a problem. A burning smell or smoke from the engine bay is a sign to stop.
issues.why: Water can get into the starter solenoid and cause a short circuit, which could start an engine-compartment fire while parked or driving.
issues.next: Park outside and away from buildings until the dealer installs the free relay kit. Check your VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: Trunk can't be opened from the inside (recall)
issues.sym: The glow-in-the-dark emergency release inside the trunk may not open the lid.
issues.why: The trunk latch can be damaged so the inside release no longer works, which breaks the federal rule meant to stop people being trapped.
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect the latch and replace the latch base for free. Check your VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: Fuel pump nozzle blockage can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Hesitation, stalling or a no-start, especially when the fuel level is low.
issues.why: On some 2021 cars with the 2.0L turbo, a leftover plastic burr from manufacturing can block a small nozzle in the fuel pump assembly and starve the engine of fuel.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free inspection and repair done.

issues.t: Hard, jerky downshifts when slowing down
issues.sym: A noticeable bump or lurch as the 8-speed automatic shifts down while you brake gently, in stop-and-go traffic or at lights. It is often worse when cold, and some owners also feel a clunk shifting out of Park.
issues.why: Owners and dealers point to the transmission's adaptive learning settling into harsh shift patterns. Genesis has released software and solenoid-related bulletins for shift quality. Some cars needed a solenoid or a full transmission replaced under warranty.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check for transmission software updates and do an adaptive reset. If the problem keeps coming back or you feel slipping, ask about the solenoid bulletin while the car is under warranty.

issues.t: Transmission slipping or gear ratio fault
issues.sym: Check engine light, flaring engine speed in gear, a feeling that the car is not fully engaged, or limp mode.
issues.why: Genesis issued bulletins for early cars on clutches slipping inside the automatic, with tests of each clutch and transmission replacement if it fails, plus bulletins for faulty solenoids or the park position switch setting codes.
issues.next: Have the codes read at a Genesis dealer and ask about the transmission bulletins. Stop driving hard on it until it is checked; these cars may still be under the powertrain warranty.

issues.t: Sunroof creaks or rattles over bumps
issues.sym: Creaking, ticking or rattling from the roof area on rough roads, mostly on cars with the wide sunroof. Some owners also hear noise near the sun visors.
issues.why: Genesis bulletins describe the wide sunroof frame and the headliner touching the roof panel, which makes noise as the body flexes.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to apply the sunroof noise bulletin. It is a comfort issue, not a safety one.

issues.t: Steering wheel shake or pulsing pedal when braking
issues.sym: A vibration in the steering wheel or brake pedal when slowing from speed.
issues.why: Genesis issued bulletins telling dealers to check and repair brake pulsation even on unsold cars, which points to rotor thickness variation from the factory or from storage.
issues.next: Have the rotors measured for runout and thickness. Resurfacing or new rotors and pads usually fixes it; on a newer car ask whether it is covered.

issues.t: Engine won't restart after auto stop-start
issues.sym: After the engine shuts off at a light using Idle Stop and Go, it does not start again when you lift off the brake, or it is slow to restart.
issues.why: A Genesis bulletin for the 2.0L turbo says low voltage at the starter's signal terminal can stop the restart.
issues.next: Restart the car with the button if it happens and have the dealer apply the bulletin. Until then you can switch stop-start off with its button.

issues.t: Connected Services app errors or dropouts
issues.sym: The Genesis app times out or fails to send remote commands, the connected features drop mid-use, or the head unit shows blank modem information.
issues.why: Genesis bulletins blame head unit software and irregular disconnections on the cellular network.
issues.next: Ask the dealer for the latest head unit software or a system reset. It does not affect driving safety.

issues.t: Radio app crashes or false 'Uneven Road Ahead' warning
issues.sym: The radio screen freezes or closes, or the cluster shows an 'Uneven Road Ahead' warning with a chime for no reason.
issues.why: Genesis issued a software bulletin for the widescreen infotainment unit used after the 2022 update.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to install the infotainment software update.

issues.t: Condensation inside the headlights
issues.sym: Fog or water droplets inside the headlight lenses, and in some cases a turn signal that stops working.
issues.why: Owners have reported moisture building up inside the headlight housings. A dealer suggested running the high beams to dry them out, which only treats the symptom.
issues.next: If the fog does not clear within a day or a bulb or signal fails, ask the dealer to check the housing seals and vents and replace the lamp under warranty.

issues.t: Head-up display too dim in bright sun
issues.sym: The windshield head-up display is hard to read on sunny days.
issues.why: Genesis issued a bulletin for 2023 G70s with a dim head-up display.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to apply the head-up display bulletin.

issues.t: Soft brake pedal from air in the brake unit
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels soft or travels further than normal before the car slows.
issues.why: A Genesis bulletin covers air trapped in the hydraulic control unit of the stability and ABS system, which needs a special bleed procedure.
issues.next: Have the brakes checked soon. Ask the dealer to bleed the hydraulic unit using the bulletin procedure.

issues.t: Check engine light for fuel rail pressure sensor
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P0191, and in some cases reduced power below highway speeds.
issues.why: Genesis released an engine computer update in 2026 for the fuel rail pressure sensor code on the 2.0L turbo.
issues.next: Ask the dealer for the engine computer update in bulletin 26-01-007G. If power loss continues after the update, ask them to check fuel pressure and the high-pressure pump.

issues.t: Rear lamp trim pieces coming loose
issues.sym: The trim pieces around the rear lights start to lift or separate from the body.
issues.why: Genesis issued a bulletin for the rear combination lamp garnishes, which can detach.
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect and replace the trim before it falls off.

issues.t: Blind-spot warning system fault
issues.sym: Blind-spot or rear cross-traffic warnings stop working, often with a warning message on the cluster.
issues.why: A Genesis bulletin traces communication faults to the rear corner radar units, which are replaced and recalibrated.
issues.next: Don't rely on the blind-spot system until it is fixed. Ask the dealer about bulletin 25-01-046G.
